svg.text: Every frame's width is a measured time. Release build, in process, one machine — the numbers are this host's, not a specification.
The paired workload, one section at a time — 7 sections

Each section is a language feature on its own: a counting loop, list indexing and in-place stores, dictionary insert and lookup, string building, method calls, recursion, and plain calls. `workload.tg <section>` runs one of them.

svg.text: The heaviest native calls, measured as they ran: len 0.045 ms, str 0.025 ms, upper 0.007 ms. These are the places a change can be measured against, because each one was timed rather than modelled.

The loop is made of what these counts say: LoadFlat 19.4%, Call 13.6%, ReturnFused 13.4%, UpdateFlatJump 9.8%, FlatJumpUnlessFlatNumber 9.7%, BinaryStoreNumber 9.6%, Constant 9.4%, FlatBinaryConstantNumber 4.3%. Over the 7 units

drawn, 538251 instructions ran; the graph has no frame per shape because what each shape costs is not measurable on this host — three attempts are recorded in `docs/performance.md`, and all three failed measurably.

Reading the two levels that are fully measured: 0.427 ms was spent parsing and lowering (the first child of every unit) against 2.628 ms of execution. For a light program the parse is most of the run; for a heavy one it is a few

The floor of a run — building an evaluator and installing the built-ins — is 1.70 µs and is the same for every program, which is why it is a frame of its own in each unit rather than folded into the execute time.
Every unit lowered to the compiled engine, so every unit has an instruction count.

Both panels together measured 3.067 ms. To regenerate: `cd tools/flamegraph && cargo run --release`. The tool sits outside the workspace, so `cargo test` at the root never builds the profiler into anything else.
a unit: one program, or one workload section
measured: the floor, parse + compile, execute
measured: a native call — a built-in, or a string method
measured: the instruction loop, whose mix of shapes is a count
measured time no child accounted for
